expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: export type Subscription = SubscriptionBase & (| { status: "trialing"; ... } | ...) — status is discriminant

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: canceled variant has only status, cancelReason, voluntary; active only has status and renewalDate — no cross-variant fields

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: function assertNever(x: never) with default: return assertNever(sub) in nextActionDate switch

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: Brands SubscriptionId, CustomerId, and PlanId using Brand<T, B> pattern

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states 'One thing not modeled here: legal transitions' and defers implementation; no constraint provided

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Names that union prevents retryCount access off active sub (compile error), assertNever catches new statuses, branded IDs prevent swaps; discusses making cancelReason a union to prevent 'voluntary: true + payment_failed'

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Opening misuse enumeration rejects flat interface with optional fields allowing nonsense like 'active + retryCount'
